name: Evolution
hook: Darwin's big idea and a century of fights — Scopes, creationism and Inherit the Wind.

facts.label: Charles Darwin
facts.statement: Charles Darwin laid out evolution by natural selection in the 1859 book On the Origin of Species, then applied it to humans in The Descent of Man.

facts.label: Alfred Russel Wallace
facts.statement: Alfred Russel Wallace arrived at natural selection independently, prompting the joint 1858 papers and pushing Darwin to publish.

facts.label: survival of the fittest
facts.statement: Herbert Spencer coined the phrase survival of the fittest, which Darwin adopted to describe natural selection.

facts.label: John Scopes
facts.statement: John Scopes was convicted and fined $100 in 1925 for teaching evolution in Dayton, Tennessee, in the so-called Monkey Trial.

facts.label: Inherit the Wind
facts.statement: Inherit the Wind, with Bertram Cates on trial, is the play and 1960 film inspired by the Scopes trial.

facts.label: creationism
facts.statement: At the Scopes trial William Jennings Bryan argued for creationism, the Christian alternative to evolution.

facts.label: intelligent design
facts.statement: In Kitzmiller v. Dover a federal judge barred a Pennsylvania district from teaching intelligent design as an alternative to evolution.
